candidates.locator: page 3, section part_i, Section 3 Pathogen Control
candidates.exact_span:
All sewage sludge that is applied to agricultural land, forest, a public contact site, or a
       reclamation site shall be treated by either the Class A or Class B pathogen requirements. Sewage
       sludge that is applied to a lawn or home garden shall be treated by the Class A pathogen
       requirements. Sewage sludge that is sold or given away in a bag shall be treated by Class A
       pathogen requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Pathogen-treatment obligations depend on how the sludge is applied or distributed (land type, lawn/home garden, bagged sale/giveaway); different readings of site classification or disposal pathway would change which Class A or Class B requirements are applicable (B) and whether expected monitoring or results should be treated as required-but-missing versus not required (C).

candidates.exact_span:
a. Six alternatives are available to demonstrate compliance with Class A sewage sludge. All 6
          options require either the density of fecal coliform in the sewage sludge be less than 1000
          Most Probable Number (MPN) per gram of total solids (dry weight basis), or the density of
          Salmonella sp. bacteria in the sewage sludge be less than three MPN per four grams of total
          solids (dry weight basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed; at the time the
          sewage sludge is prepared for sale or given away in a bag or other container for application
          to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage sets universal Class A numeric thresholds for fecal coliform and Salmonella, specifies dry-weight basis and timing triggers (use/disposal vs bag preparation); interpreting the disjunctive limit structure, units, or applicable timing would change enforceable limit selection and exceedance evaluation (A) and when monitoring or sampling is obligated (B).

candidates.exact_span:
A sludge. Alternatives 5 and 6 are not authorized to demonstrate compliance with Class A
          sewage sludge in Texas permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The Texas-specific prohibition on Alternatives 5 and 6 restricts which Class A demonstration pathways are permit-authorized; interpreting permit jurisdiction or which alternative was used would change which numeric limits and treatment demonstrations count as valid compliance evidence (A) and which monitoring or recordkeeping pathways are applicable (B).

candidates.exact_span:
Alternative 1 - The temperature of the sewage sludge that is used or disposed shall be
           maintained at a specific value for a period of time. See 503.32(a)(3)(ii) for specific
           information.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 1 makes Class A compliance contingent on a temperature-duration treatment demonstration tied to external 503.32 specifications; interpreting whether this alternative is selected, what 'used or disposed' means, or how the cross-reference incorporates numeric criteria would change which monitoring and treatment records are required (B).

candidates.exact_span:
Alternative 2 - The pH of the sewage sludge that is used or disposed shall be raised to above
           12 and shall remain above 12 for 72 hours. The pH shall be defined as the logarithm of the
           reciprocal of the hydrogen ion concentration measured at 25 degrees Celsius or measured at
           another temperature and then converted to an equivalent value at 25 degrees Celsius.
           The temperature of the sewage sludge shall be above 52 degrees Celsius for 12 hours or
           longer during the period that the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12.
           At the end of the 72 hour period during which the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12, the
           sewage sludge shall be air dried to achieve a percent solids in the sewage sludge greater than
           50%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 2 embeds multiple numeric compliance thresholds (pH > 12 for 72 hours, temperature > 52°C for 12 hours, percent solids > 50%) plus measurement definitions and sequencing; different interpretations of pH measurement method, duration overlap, or solids percentage would change limit exceedance determinations (A) and required process monitoring (B).

candidates.exact_span:
Alternative 3 - The sewage sludge shall be analyzed for enteric viruses prior to pathogen
           treatment. The limit for enteric viruses is one Plaque-forming Unit per four grams of total
           solids (dry weight basis) either before or following pathogen treatment. See 503.32(a)(5)(ii)
           for specific information.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 3 imposes a mandatory enteric-virus analysis with a numeric limit of 1 PFU per four grams dry weight and allows sampling before or after treatment; interpreting sampling timing, dry-weight basis, or cross-referenced details would change numeric compliance comparison (A), whether virus monitoring is required (B), and how absent or non-numeric virus results are classified when evidence is incomplete (C).
